outcomes.statement: Operations on, and compositions of, functions.
Effects of horizontal and vertical translations on graphs and equations.
Effects of horizontal and vertical stretches on graphs and equations.
Apply translations and stretches to graphs and equations.
Effects of reflections in the x-axis, y-axis and the line y = x.
Inverses of relations.
Logarithms.
Product, quotient and power laws of logarithms.
Graph and analyze exponential and logarithmic functions.
Solve problems involving exponential and logarithmic equations.
Factor polynomials of degree > 2 (degree ≤ 5, integral coefficients).
Graph and analyze polynomial functions (degree ≤ 5).
Graph and analyze radical functions (one radical).
Graph and analyze rational functions (monomial, binomial, trinomial numerators/denominators).
Angles in standard position in degrees and radians.
Develop and apply the equation of the unit circle.
Solve problems using the six trigonometric ratios (degrees and radians).
Graph and analyze sine, cosine and tangent to solve problems.
Solve first- and second-degree trigonometric equations algebraically and graphically.
Prove trigonometric identities (reciprocal, quotient, Pythagorean, sum/difference, double-angle).
Apply the fundamental counting principle.
Permutations of n elements taken r at a time.
Combinations of n different elements taken r at a time.
Expand powers of a binomial, including the binomial theorem (natural-number exponents).

misconceptions.description: Multiplies powers by multiplying exponents or adds bases (a^m·a^n = a^(mn)).
Treats a negative exponent as a negative number (a^-n = -a^n).
Swaps numerator and denominator of a rational exponent (a^(m/n) read as m-th root of a^n).
Adds radicands: √a + √b = √(a+b).
Multiplies by the wrong conjugate or forgets to multiply the numerator.
Stops factoring early (common factor left, or a difference of squares left unfactored).
Factors a sum of squares as (a+b)(a−b) or (a+b)².
Sign error in binomial factors of a trinomial.
Uses −b incorrectly or divides only part of the numerator by 2a.
Reads the vertex of y = a(x − h)² + k as (−h, k).
Finds non-permissible values only after cancelling, losing restrictions.
Cancels terms rather than factors ((x+3)/3 = x).
Keeps a root that fails the original equation (or a non-permissible value).
Rejects a valid root, often a negative one, as extraneous.
Squares a binomial as a² + b² (forgets the middle term).
Reads f(x) as f times x, or f(a+b) as f(a)+f(b).
Uses a square bracket at an excluded endpoint or at infinity, or swaps set/interval notation.
Swaps domain and range.
Reflects the whole graph instead of only the part below the x-axis.
Measures the reference angle from the y-axis.
Adds exponents for a power of a power ((a^m)^n = a^(m+n)).
Applies an exponent to the variable but not the coefficient ((2x)^3 = 2x^3).
Ignores a negative exponent or takes the reciprocal of only part of the expression.
Multiplies the base by the exponent (8^(2/3) = 16/3).
Takes the root but not the power of a rational exponent (or the power but not the root).
Leaves a perfect-square factor under the root or extracts a factor that is not a perfect square.
Combines radicals that are not like terms, or adds coefficients incorrectly.
Drops the common factor (or a sign) when factoring it out.
Writes a difference of squares as a perfect square (a − b)².
Ignores the leading coefficient when factoring ax² + bx + c.
Takes the roots of (x − r)(x − s) = 0 as −r and −s.
Misreads the discriminant (negative means two roots, or zero means none).
Takes only the positive square root when solving x² = k.
Adds b instead of (b/2)² when completing the square, or forgets to factor out a first.
Calls the vertex a minimum when a < 0, or a maximum when a > 0.
Swaps the coordinates of the vertex, or reads k as the x-coordinate.
Confuses f(a) (evaluate at a) with f(x) = a (solve for x).
Drops brackets when substituting a negative value ((−3)² taken as −9).
Reads the value from the wrong row or column of a table.
Ignores whether an endpoint on a graph is open or closed.
Misses a restriction from a square root or a denominator.
Computes slope as run over rise (Δx/Δy).
Reads the intercept or the point in an equation with the wrong sign.
Uses the negative slope, not the negative reciprocal, for a perpendicular line.
Treats |a − b| as |a| − |b|, or lets an absolute value be negative.
Splits y = |f(x)| at the wrong x-value instead of the zero of f.
Adds fractions by adding numerators and adding denominators.
Flips the wrong fraction when dividing, or forgets to flip.
Takes zeros of the numerator as non-permissible values.
Subtracts only the first term of the second numerator (the minus sign is not distributed).
Multiplies only some terms by the lowest common denominator.
Squares both sides before isolating the radical.
Reports only one intersection point, or only the x-values.
Makes a sign or distribution error when setting the expressions equal.
Uses θ − 180° in quadrant II or 180° − θ in quadrant III.
Swaps sine and cosine exact values (sin 30° = √3/2).
Uses x/r for sine or y/r for cosine, or x/y for tangent.
Uses the sine law when the cosine law is needed, or the reverse.
Uses + 2bc cos A in the cosine law, or multiplies the whole of b² + c² − 2bc by cos A.
Pairs a side with an angle that is not opposite it.
Moves the graph in the wrong horizontal direction (sign of h).
Moves the graph in the wrong vertical direction.
Horizontal stretch by b instead of 1/b (mapping x → bx).
Applies a to x-coordinates or b to y-coordinates.
Translates before stretching/reflecting when mapping points (x/b + h computed as (x+h)/b).
Reads h from f(bx − c) as c instead of c/b.
Confuses reflection in the x-axis (y → −y) with the y-axis (x → −x).
Believes invariant points only exist for reflections, or misses those on the line of stretch.
Looks for invariant points on the wrong axis (y-intercepts for a vertical stretch).
Writes mapping notation with the wrong form or order.
Treats f⁻¹(x) as 1/f(x).
Writes y = f⁻¹(x) for an inverse that is not a function.
Restricts the domain on the wrong side of the vertex, or restricts the range instead.
Swaps x and y but solves incorrectly (e.g. takes only the positive root without restriction).
Combines a reflection in y = x with other transformations in the wrong order.
Computes g(f(x)) instead of f(g(x)).
Multiplies f(x)·g(x) instead of composing.
Uses only one function's domain for f+g, f·g, etc.
Forgets to exclude zeros of the divisor from the domain of a quotient.
Finds the domain of f(g(x)) from the simplified formula only, ignoring the domain of g.
Adds x-coordinates instead of y-coordinates when combining graphs.
Combines the outputs with the wrong operation (adds instead of multiplies, or the reverse).
Divides or subtracts in the wrong order (g/f instead of f/g, g − f instead of f − g).
Uses +a instead of −a (or vice versa) as the synthetic divisor.
Omits a zero placeholder for a missing power.
Evaluates P(−a) for division by (x − a).
Tests factors of the leading coefficient instead of the constant term.
Mixes up crossing vs touching: thinks even multiplicity crosses.
Determines end behaviour from the constant term or first factor, not from the degree and leading coefficient.
Takes the y-intercept as the product of zeros without the leading coefficient or signs.
Writes the factor of zero x = a as (x + a).
Reports a local maximum as the absolute maximum.
Counts the number of factors rather than summing multiplicities to get the degree.
Mishandles the remainder or quotient in the division statement (drops the divisor under R, or reads dividend coefficients as the quotient).
Takes the constant term (or the sum of the coefficients) as the remainder.
Lists only some divisors of the constant term (misses negatives, ±1 or the constant itself).
Subtracts the cut-out square once instead of twice from each dimension.
Accepts a sketch without checking end behaviour, every zero's behaviour and the y-intercept.
Writes log(A + B) = log A + log B.
Writes log A / log B = log(A/B) or log(A − B).
Applies the power law to a coefficient or to part of the argument ((log x)² = 2 log x).
Condenses before moving coefficients into exponents.
Converts log_b(x) = y to x^y = b or y^b = x.
Accepts log of a negative number or zero.
Inverts the change-of-base ratio.
Puts the horizontal asymptote at y = 0 after a vertical translation, or the vertical asymptote of a log at x = 0 after a horizontal translation.
Believes b < 1 gives growth.
Multiplies the coefficient into the base (2·3^x = 6^x).
Forgets to bring the whole exponent (binomial) down in brackets.
Swaps t and p, or uses the rate instead of the factor b (1.05 vs 0.05).
Uses an annual rate without dividing by the number of compounding periods.
Subtracts intensities instead of finding a ratio (or vice versa) on log scales.
Uses degree values in a radian context (or calculator in wrong mode).
Multiplies by 180/π when converting degrees to radians.
Adds 180° instead of 360° for coterminal angles.
Writes a general solution with the wrong period (2πn for a tangent, or πn where 2πn needed).
Uses degrees in a = rθ.
Swaps cos and sin coordinates (P(θ) = (sin θ, cos θ)).
Wrong sign from CAST for the quadrant.
Gives the reference angle instead of the angle in the required quadrant.
Treats csc θ as sin⁻¹θ.
Mixes up √3/2 and 1/2 for π/6 and π/3.
Uses period = b or b/2π instead of 2π/|b|.
Reads phase shift from sin(bx − c) as c rather than c/b.
Takes amplitude as max − min (not half).
Uses the max (or the average of non-extrema) as the midline.
Places tan asymptotes at multiples of π instead of π/2 + πn.
Finds one solution only and misses the second quadrant solution.
Lists solutions outside the given domain or misses them at the boundary.
Divides both sides by a trig factor, losing solutions.
Confuses sin 2x with 2 sin x or sin²x.
Picks the wrong cos 2x form, leaving mixed functions.
Moves terms across the equal sign while proving (treats an identity as an equation).
Thinks checking one value proves an identity.
Misses non-permissible values from a denominator or from tan/sec/csc/cot.
Writes sin(A + B) = sin A + sin B.
Multiplies only the denominator by the conjugate.
Writes 1 − tan²θ = sec²θ or similar sign errors.
Writes 'sin' without its argument.
Uses invariant points other than y = 0 and y = 1 for y = √f(x).
Keeps the regions where f(x) < 0 in the domain of √f(x).
Believes √f(x) < f(x) everywhere (forgets 0 < f(x) < 1).
Draws a vertical asymptote where a factor cancels (point of discontinuity).
Calls a non-cancelling zero of the denominator a hole.
Finds the horizontal asymptote from constant terms instead of leading coefficients/degree.
Forgets to exclude the y-value of the hole from the range.
Forgets to exclude the x-value of the hole from the domain.
Reads x-intercepts from the denominator.
Lists the cancelled factor's zero as an x-intercept.
Adds where 'and' requires multiplication, or multiplies 'or' cases.
Fills the constrained slot last instead of first.
Simplifies n!/(n−2)! as n or n/2 or similar.
Uses permutations when order does not matter (or vice versa).
Forgets to multiply by internal arrangements of a block.
Computes 'apart' directly with errors instead of total − together.
Forgets to divide by factorials of identical items.
Double-counts overlapping cases.
Keeps a negative or non-integer n, or n < r.
Computes 'at least one' by fixing one item then choosing freely (overcounts).
Uses k for the k-th term instead of k − 1 (t_k vs t_(k+1)).
Forgets to raise the coefficient (or sign) of a term to its power.
Mis-tracks exponents when terms are non-linear (x² or 1/x).
Uses row n+1 or n−1 of Pascal's triangle.
Thinks (x + y)^n has n terms.
Drops the alternating sign for (x − y)^n.
Writes an expression when an equation is required.
Omits units in a final answer.
Omits necessary brackets (e.g. −3² vs (−3)², log x + 2 vs log(x + 2)).
Sketch missing scaled axes or key features (intercepts, asymptotes, endpoints, max/min).
Answers a different directing word (e.g. verifies when asked to prove, decimal when exact asked).
Window omits a key feature, or wrong window format.
Calculator in the wrong angle mode.
Sets left/right bounds that do not bracket the zero/intersection.
Rounds intermediate values or rounds to the wrong place.
